evidence: independent audit of numerical-uncalibrated simulations and literature/web checks; not a physical test

severityScale.fatal: kills the concept as specified; no credible design change inside the concept keeps it
severityScale.major: a claimed pass or key assumption does not hold; fixable by a design/model change

findings.claim: Claim: the canopy flies stably at L/D≈0.5 while depowered to CR 0.2, giving ~5 N pull and a ~41° view. The whole footage/pull result rests on one point of the ASSUMED coefficient envelope, and that point is a soft canopy that is both depowered (low AoA) and parachutal (L/D<1) at the same time.
findings.evidence: out_kite2.json scenarios.*.audit.filmOperatingPoint: while filming, CR is pinned at CRmin=0.2 for 100 % of the time in nominal, fast and gust, with median L/D G=0.68 (nominal), 0.64 (fast), 0.73 (gust) and median CL≈0.11. L/D is below 0.8 for 65 % (nominal) and 81 % (fast) of the time. Literature: soft ram-air or gliding-parachute canopies reach L/D≤1 only at high AoA, where the resultant coefficient is ~0.8–1.1. NASA's five-lobe gliding parachute (Ware & Libbey 1968, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19680018975/downloads/19680018975.pdf) has maximum lift near 25° AoA and L/D falling from 2.2 to ~0 over 22.5–90°. Parafoil wind-tunnel data (https://apps.dtic.mil/sti/pdfs/AD0731564.pdf) give CLmax 0.75–1.0 and L/Dmax 1.8–6.4. Soft wings lose internal pressure and luff or tuck at low AoA (https://www.surfertoday.com/kiteboarding/how-does-a-kite-fly; hooded-kite patent https://patents.google.com/patent/US4243191). The model treats CR and G as independent actuators. Sensitivity (out_kite2.json envelope): with CRmin 0.4, gust body force is 53.9 N (FAIL >40), gust avail 68.7 % (FAIL) and fast body force 33.6 N. With CRmin 0.6, nominal avail is 62 % (FAIL), fast 51 N and gust 69 N. With CRmin 0.8, nominal avail is 49.8 % and gust force 89 N. With Gmin 1.0 (sled-like), the view elevation is 50.7° nominal and 53.8° fast, failing the concept's own ≤50° gate. Closed form: holding 5 N needs CR 0.198 at 12 m/s and 0.088 at 18 m/s. At a parachutal CR of 0.9 the pull would be 22.7 N at 12 m/s and 51 N at 18 m/s.
findings.recommendedFix: Couple CR and L/D through one AoA polar, plus a separate drag device or reefing, instead of two free actuators. Depower by area (reefing or a variable-span arc) rather than by AoA. Re-run every scenario on a polar measured by tow-testing a 0.35 m² single-skin canopy (CR and L/D vs AoA, plus the collapse boundary). Treat it as fatal if the tow test shows CR ≥~0.5 at L/D ≤0.8.

findings.claim: Claim: the flying mass is 62 g (canopy + KCU with 3 actuators, IMU/GNSS/UWB/pitot and a fail-safe spring + 4K camera + cell). The concept's own itemisation already sums to 68 g, and a component-based budget gives 75–113 g. The fast-scenario KE margin then disappears.
findings.evidence: index.js mass note: 24+3+12+16+8+5 = 68 g, but the param v is 0.062. RunCam Thumb Pro: 16–16.5 g and 500 mA@5 V (2.5 W) confirmed (https://www.getfpv.com/runcam-thumb-pro-4k-hd-action-camera.html). It ships with a wide lens, so the 60° rectilinear optic that sets pxMed is a custom ASSUMED part. A 10–12 g KCU with three line-load actuators (brake/depower lines carry an estimated 20–40 % of 5–22 N), MCU+IMU+GNSS+UWB+pitot and a fail-safe spring is not credible. The audit estimate is 18–30 g, and the canopy 25–40 g for ~0.47 m² flat single-skin at 33 g/m² plus ribs and reinforcements; Flysurfer Peak 6 m² is 0.98 kg kite-only (https://flysurfer.com/project/peak2/). Dynamics re-run (out_kite2.json massSensitivity): fast keMax is 12.94 J at 62 g, 14.07 J at 68 g, 17.31 J at 85 g (FAIL) and 20.16 J at 100 g (FAIL); stopstart is 14.56 J at 100 g. Min flying airspeed is 2.11 → 2.47 m/s at 85 g. The kite reaches 20.4 m/s ground speed in the fast scenario.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the 68 g own budget as the minimum. Publish a component-level BOM with sourced masses. Cap the ground-frame kite speed (shorter line or lower station in fast mode) or the rider speed for filming at ~16 m/s, so that KE ≤14.9 J at ≥85 g.

findings.claim: Claim: the kite 'never launches while stationary' and the lift ride needs 0 actions. In fact an armed, docked kite auto-launches on a chairlift or T-bar, and the 'armed' state is never cleared by docking.
findings.evidence: model.js l.250: launch fires when armed && rider speed >4 m/s && apparent air from ahead for 0.5 s. There is no climb, lift or geofence check. stopstart shows that a dock keeps the kite armed (automatic relaunch). Audit sim (out_kite2.json liftInterlock) puts a docked, armed kite on a rider at 5 m/s, the line speed of a detachable chair, and it launches at t=1.0 s. T-bars run 2.5–4 m/s. Pistes often pass under lift lines, with chairs 3–10 m above the snow, and the kite flies 4–5 m up on a 7 m line. modelLimits says 'never near lifts', but nothing enforces this.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a launch inhibit unless altitude is decreasing (baro/GNSS descent) and the rider is not in a lift geofence. Auto-disarm at every dock or count a 'disarm' tap, which makes the honest ops 2 per run. Add an overhead-lift geofence that forces retrieve.

findings.claim: Claim: others are protected by the 22 N clutch and slide-off. In reality the 0.5 mm, essentially invisible UHMWPE line runs at chest-to-neck height through the zone directly behind the rider, which is exactly where an overtaking uphill skier passes. Only one crossing geometry was simulated, with an ASSUMED slide-off.
findings.evidence: Audit line height above the snow (nominal, while filming): 1 m behind min 1.15 m (lineH1m); 2 m behind p5 1.72 m, median 2.33 m (out_kite2.json lineHeightBehind_m). In the gust run the 2 m p5 is 1.75 m, in tail 1.68 m. The 'cross' scenario uses a single 0.35 m-behind crossing at 8 m/s with contact at h=1.9 m (helmet/raised pole) and an ASSUMED slide-off after 1.0 m. Neck or face contact (h 1.4–1.7 m), a skier coming up from behind along the line, and wrap-around are not modelled. Thin taut braid sliding across skin at 8–15 m/s closing speed is a laceration hazard, whatever the 22 N clutch does.
findings.recommendedFix: Raise the line exit with a light telescoping mast or exit boom (+0.6–0.8 m), so that the line is >2.2 m above the snow by 1 m behind. Put a high-visibility sheath on the first ~4 m. Add a weak-link breakaway (≤10 N) at the pack plus a cutter. Simulate overtaking and neck-height contacts. Restrict use to low-traffic runs.

findings.claim: Regulation and resort rules: the safe-use envelope depends on permission that resorts commonly withhold. Aviation law is light for a <1 kg kite, but resort rules (kiting and drone bans) block most pistes.
findings.evidence: Aspen Skiing Co. bans kiting activities (kite skiing, traction kites, speed gliding) within operating boundaries (https://www.aspensnowmass.com/four-mountains/buttermilk/mountain-regulations-buttermilk). Niseko Grand Hirafu bans snow kites and anything flying over or affecting its slopes and lifts (https://www.grand-hirafu.jp/winter/en/gelande/). Big White bans public drone use (https://bigwhite.com/node/1344). EU: the EASA FAQ says tethered free-flight aircraft such as kites fall under the UAS Regulation only above 25 kg (https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/print/pdf/node/132034/185706). An autonomously steered KCU could still be argued to make it an unmanned aircraft, which would put it in open category/C0 territory. UK CAA has a separate tethered-UA ≤1 kg provision (https://www.caa.co.uk/drones/rules-and-categories-of-drone-flying/tethered-drones-and-remotely-piloted-aircraft/). FAA Part 101 Subpart B covers only kites >5 lb, so a 62–100 g kite is outside it.
findings.recommendedFix: Get a written per-resort permission strategy. Position the product for permitted terrain: private or club slopes, backcountry, and resorts that permit it. Make permission checking part of the product (a geofenced allow-list).

findings.claim: Claim: calm stops auto-dock 48/48 and the standstill is ≤7.4 s. That result holds only at the scenario's very low calm turbulence (σ=0.2 m/s). Docking degrades with modest turbulence and with head- or tail-wind stops, and the KCU contacts the helmet in some runs. The physical douse of a wet canopy with bridle and 3 control lines into a 2 L sleeve has no precedent at this scale.
findings.evidence: Audit calm-stop sweep, 96 runs per level (out_kite2.json calmDockVsTurbulence): manual push-in needed in 1/96 runs at σ 0.2 m/s, 10/96 at 0.4, 14/96 at 0.5 and 19/96 at 0.7. Stop grid with 0–4.4 m/s winds from the side, ahead and behind (out_kite2.json stops): 56/96 auto-docked, 25 manual, 15 not stowed within ~14 s (3 retries exhausted or parked). KCU-to-helmet clearance ≤0 in 4 runs, minimum −0.083 m. The concept's own demo stops are 2/5 manual, with clearance −0.01 m. Docking success in the model is judged only by approach angle (≤80°). The auto-launch/recovery precedents are a SkySails mast and Kitepower's launch setup, both large and supervised.
findings.recommendedFix: Add an approach-path planner that keeps the KCU out of a 0.3 m helmet keep-out zone, a retry policy that ends in a safe park or flagged landing, and a dock/douse cycle test (≥500 cycles: wet, iced, gusty). Count a manual push-in as +1 action and a 15–20 s standstill. Audit p90 standstill with a 15 s manual push-in is 17 s, which still passes ≤30 s.

findings.claim: The stated envelope ('no tailwind exceeding skier speed −3 m/s') is not safe. Short turns with a modest quartering tailwind inside that envelope lose the kite onto the snow.
findings.evidence: Audit wind cases (out_kite2.json windCases): short turns with a 6 m/s quartering tail (4.2 m/s along-track, inside the stated envelope at 8 m/s) give avail 4.3 % and the kite lands. Short turns with a 9 m/s tail give avail 16 % and the kite lands. Nominal carving with the same winds stays at 93–96 %. The scenario set has a tailwind case only for 12 m/s carving.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a short-turn/tailwind scenario to the set. Use a park/retrieve rule based on the predicted apparent-wind margin, and give an honest envelope (e.g. tailwind component ≤ 0.3 × rider speed).

findings.claim: Nominal is a 30 s continuous carve with no stops. Every push-off costs ~2.5 s before the kite is on station, so availability over a realistic run with stops is below 80 %. This is disclosed, but nominal is not representative.
findings.evidence: stopstart avail 76.9 % (FAIL, reproduced), 73.1–74.0 % at 85–100 g. Nominal 92.4 %.
findings.recommendedFix: Report a 'whole run' scenario (3–5 stops over 2–3 min) as the headline avail. Pre-launch at walking speed if the launch path allows.

findings.claim: On steep, slow terrain (24° moguls at 4.5 m/s) the minimum cone angle forces a near top-down view.
findings.evidence: Moguls viewElev 53.2° (FAIL ≤50, disclosed). With 6 seeds at 3 m/s crosswind it is 49.3–52.0°. Avail stays at 100 %.
findings.recommendedFix: Accept as an envelope limit, or use a longer line on steep slopes.

findings.claim: Launch and inflation happen from the pack top, inside the rider's body wake, with the KCU ejected about 0.3 m from the helmet. The wake is not modelled (disclosed).
findings.evidence: Launch requires apparent wind from ahead (model.js l.249), so the pack is in the separated wake of the head and torso. The model starts inflation at 0.05 and reaches full inflation in 0.7 s with no wake deficit.
findings.recommendedFix: Eject the KCU upward on a spring mast above the wake. Model a wake velocity deficit (e.g. 50 % within 1 m behind the head).

findings.claim: Endurance of 258 min is credible only if the kite's 1.3 Wh cell recharges in the dock (contacts not designed). The kite sortie has little margin.
findings.evidence: Recomputed: (30+1.3) Wh × 0.75 (−10 °C) × 0.9 (reserve) × 60 / 4.91 W = 258 min, which reproduces the claim. Sortie: 1.3 × 0.675 × 60 / 3.4 W = 15.5 min. The camera draw of 2.5 W is the vendor maximum (500 mA@5 V). At 3.5 W the sortie is 12 min, below the concept's own 15 min gate. The cold factor of 0.75 is reasonable for a pack cell but optimistic for an unheated 8 g cell in 12 m/s airflow.
findings.recommendedFix: Design the dock charging contacts or inductive link. Size the kite cell for 20 min at 3.5 W and −10 °C.

findings.claim: Fault scenarios judged on safety only hide real losses: the snag leaves line and kite in the tree, and kcu_fail and cut lose most of the run's footage.
findings.evidence: snag: body force 28 N (pass ≤40); leftOnObstacle = line and kite left at the tree; avail 39.6 %; subject jitter 8.2 °/s. kcu_fail avail 33.7 %, body force 18.6 N. cut avail 41.2 %. All of these are flagged 'not judged'.
findings.recommendedFix: Report the recovery cost (a walk or climb to the tree, kite lost) as an ops/time penalty in the safety summary.

findings.claim: Unplanned stop is handled by 'land beside + snow pull' with ≤17.9 s standstill in 0–9 m/s wind (stop_wind passes).
findings.evidence: stop_wind uses wind seed 5, one of the favourable seeds. Same scenario, seeds 1–12: 6/12 end with the hip cutter firing (line paid out to the 25 m spool end while the 95 g glider kites downwind instead of landing); airMin 0.877–1.65 Vs; line touches the rider's body in 10/12 and a pole in 7/12. Wider sweep (stop, 0/3/6/9 m/s × 4 directions × 4 seeds, 52 runs): cut/release 0/4, 0/16, 1/16, 8/16; airMin <1 Vs in 9 runs; harmonised p90 standstill = 21 s with the model's own hard-coded 21 s 'manual pick-up', 120 s if a loose glider ≥25 m downwind costs 120 s (ASSUMED). After a cut the glider stays hooked and free-flies trailing up to 25 m of 0.17 mm line across the piste. audit/out_towglider.json seedSweep.stop_wind, audit/out_towglider_stopsweep.json.
findings.recommendedFix: In mean wind >5 m/s: on stop, dive to the snow immediately (full split flaps, nose down) instead of the 'recover' glide; retract at full winch rate while still airborne; release the hook BEFORE any hip cut so no line trails the glider; report the seed sweep, not one seed.

findings.claim: 95 g all-up glider incl. 4K camera 16 g and a 12 g 2-axis micro gimbal (mass_budget_g in design_notes).
findings.evidence: No 12 g gimbal able to carry a 16 g 4K camera was found. The smallest brushless 2-axis FPV gimbal found is the Caddx GM2 at 30 g, for 19 mm micro cameras (https://rotorama.com/product/gm2). The XF C-40D is 38 g. Lighter mounts are servo pan/tilt and do not stabilise. Wiring/connectors/5 V boost/SD (~4 g) and the tow-release and fold-latch actuators (~2 g) are not budgeted. Audit estimate 115–125 g. At 117 g with CLmax 0.9 and CD0 0.05: Vs 6.81 m/s (claimed 5.82), KE-cap speed 15.799 m/s (claimed 17.4–17.7). 16 m/s run: hook release, avail 21.982 %. Slow 6 m/s beginner: airMin 0.086 Vs, minimum height 0.035 m (snow contact), jitter 44.66 °/s, avail 33.494 %. dock_wind KE 16.158 J (>14.9). Nominal still passes (avail 88.422 %, KE 13.802 J).
findings.recommendedFix: Budget a real gimbal (≥25–30 g), or drop to a single-axis tilt with wide-sensor EIS (the cam_fixed90 variant failed, so this needs a new study). Then resize the wing (S≈0.065–0.07 m²) to keep Vs ≤6 m/s and re-run all scenarios at 120 g.

findings.claim: Endurance 102 min at −10 °C (glider 1.2 Wh topped up from the 10 Wh hip cell on every lift ride).
findings.evidence: Running the RunCam Thumb Pro 4K (16 g) at 2.5 W max at 5 V (https://www.getfpv.com/runcam-thumb-pro-4k-hd-action-camera.html) through a boost converter, the audit avionics total is 4.441 W, against 3.3 W claimed. Glider-only flight: 10.944 min (claimed 14.7). A 4 min run uses 0.296 Wh, so an 8 min lift must recharge at about 1.85 C. Li-ion/LiPo must not be charged below about 0 °C because lithium plates (https://www.redarcelectronics.com/us/resources/chargers-isolators-faqs/do-not-charge-lithium-battery-below-32-degrees/). A −10 °C holster blocks the top-up, so the day is limited to about 11 min of flight. A heated holster and cell at the audit power gives 79.102 min.
findings.recommendedFix: Heat the holster and glider cell from the hip cell (+~1 W while docked), or fly the glider on a hip-cell supply fed through the leash (a conductive line adds mass and visibility), or fit a 2–3 Wh glider cell (+8–12 g). Re-state endurance with the real camera power.

findings.claim: Envelope: carving and short turns pass on 15°; ≤~17 m/s; wind 5 m/s head/tail and 9 m/s gusty crosswind pass.
findings.evidence: The concept did not run the calibrated shared presets. Expert carve, 20°, 13 m/s: avail 73.535 % (FAIL <80), pxMed 389.969. Steep 28°, 15 m/s: avail 37.635 %, KE 15.336 J (FAIL >14.9). Tailwind 5 m/s over 12 seeds: avail min 74.1 % (1 FAIL), airMin <1 Vs in 2/12 (stall in the model). Moguls 24° at 4.5 m/s pass (avail 90.092 %). 16 m/s at 95 g passes (100 %).
findings.recommendedFix: State the envelope as 10–18° pistes and 6–16 m/s (95 g) or 8–15 m/s (≈120 g). Add the expertCarve and steep presets to the scenario set. For steep slopes, use a larger brake ΔCD or a higher station to burn energy.

findings.claim: Per-run user cost: ops 2 (arm + dock tap), standstill p90 17.9 s, handsBusy 0.4 %.
findings.evidence: The nominal scenario contains no stop, no launch and no dock; these are judged in separate runs, and setupTime is a single worst event, not a per-run sum. The model has no docked→launch transition, so after an unplanned rest stop the glider stays seated until it is re-armed: ops = 2 + number of rest stops. One rest stop: ops 3, standstill 1 + 15.5–21 + 1 s. Two rest stops: about 35–44 s (FAIL ≤30). In the hook-release cases (rider >17 m/s, snag, crossing) the glider lands for manual pick-up: fast lagMax 89.9 m upslope, yet setupTime is reported as the constant 17.9 s. design_notes says 30–120 s ASSUMED.
findings.recommendedFix: Auto-relaunch at the next push-off while the run is armed, and disarm with the lift-base geofence (ops → 1 + 0). Report standstill per realistic run (2 rest stops plus the final dock), and count release pick-ups at a walking speed uphill.

findings.claim: Regulation: <250 g, EU C0/A1 follow-me ≤50 m; the US position is unresolved.
findings.evidence: EU: follow-me within 50 m is allowed in A1 (https://www.oesterreich.gv.at/de/themen/reisen_und_freizeit/Drohnen/Drohnenkategorien_open_specific_certified). A privately built drone under 250 g that carries a camera and is not a toy still needs operator registration (https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/the-agency/faqs/open-category); design_notes omits this. US: 49 USC 44809 requires VLOS by the operator or by a co-located visual observer in direct communication (https://pilotinstitute.com/drone-vlos-rules/). A solo rider facing downhill cannot meet that, and a hook-release free flight is plainly a UA rather than a kite. Resorts: Vail Resorts bans all drone use, hobbyists and filming included, on or over its land, also on USFS land (https://www.vail.com/the-mountain/about-the-mountain/safety/drones.aspx).
findings.recommendedFix: Treat it as EU/UK A1-only with registration. Seek written resort permission. For the US, a Part 107 §107.31 waiver or a kite classification would require that it never free-flies, which conflicts with the hook-release safety design.

findings.claim: Leash safety: 3 N clutch cap, the line clears head height beyond 1.6 m behind the hip, and a crossing skier feels ≤1.85 N.
findings.evidence: The crossing case is modelled well (1.85 N, hook release in 0.1 s). Not covered: (a) the smoothed station lags the rider laterally (lagMax 10.715 m in nominal), so for most of the time a near-invisible line sweeps across the piste between 1 and 3.5 m height; (b) after an unplanned stop, 10–20 m of line lies over the piste uphill of the stopped rider for 15–21 s while the glider is pulled in; (c) the cut case leaves a free glider trailing up to 25 m of line (TG-01); (d) the line touches the rider's body or a pole in many wind-stop runs (16/52 and 8/52). Laceration is judged only by contact pressure (0.9 MPa); sliding a 0.17 mm braid across skin at 5–10 m/s is not assessed.
findings.recommendedFix: Use a 1–2 m sheathed hi-vis leader at the hip and pennants every 2–3 m. Always release the hook before cutting. Sense line strikes (tension-rate spike → free pay-out). Keep the station within ±2 m of the rider's track when others are within 20 m (UWB/vision).

findings.claim: In-motion dock through the skier wake: seated 4.5 s before the stop at 0.9–1.3 m/s relative.
findings.evidence: The final approach runs at about 2 m/s airspeed (≈0.35 Vs) in an 85 % wake deficit, so the glider is an unstable towed body. The model treats it as a point mass with no attitude dynamics, in a turbulence-free far-wake similarity deficit, captured when the hook comes within 9 cm of the funnel; the wings fold only below 0.55 m of line. A skier's wake sheds at roughly St≈0.2 → 0.2·12/0.5 ≈ 5 Hz with large velocity fluctuations. Capture reliability is therefore unknown, not 100 % (52/52 dock runs succeed in the model by construction).
findings.recommendedFix: Treat the dock as unverified. Use land + snow pull as the baseline. Plan a bench and tow test of capture in a wake; consider folding the wings before entering the wake (≥2 m) and drawing the folded dart in.

findings.claim: jitterRms 0.52 °/s (footageStability subject 0.97, background 1.12 °/s nominal) with a 2-axis micro gimbal.
findings.evidence: The gimbal is an ideal 3 Hz world-frame LOS tracker plus a 0.5 °/s residual; the glider has no attitude dynamics (3-DOF point mass), so turbulence-driven rotation of a 95 g airframe never reaches the gimbal. Roll is levelled electronically at bank angles up to 50°. The pass is plausible for a real brushless gimbal, but this model cannot falsify it.
findings.recommendedFix: Add rigid-body attitude (roll/pitch response to gusts) and a gimbal plant with a finite disturbance-rejection bandwidth, then re-run.

findings.claim: Test 'dt-converged core' and the convergence claim.
findings.evidence: The sub-step count is KS = max(6, …) and the floor of 6 dominates, so subFactor 1, 2 and 4 give bit-identical outputs (position rms difference 0 m in nominal, short and gust). The test compares identical runs, and the 50 Hz controller and sample step are never refined.
findings.recommendedFix: Make KS scale with subFactor (KS = 6·kFac) and add a run at controller step 0.01 s.

findings.claim: results.json is the record of the current model.
findings.evidence: The gust row is stale. dev/towglider/results.json has avail 88.353, bodyForcePeak 1.576 N, tensionP95 0.818 N and towShare 48.7 %; a fresh run of the same code gives 88.491, 0.826, 0.617 and 37.8 %. The other 19 scenarios match exactly. The model is deterministic: two runs gave identical output.
findings.recommendedFix: Re-run run_all.mjs after every model edit; add a hash of the model files to results.json.

findings.claim: keMax ≤14.2 J everywhere (fast 13.8 J).
findings.evidence: The 1 s settle window excludes t<1 s from keMax. In the fast scenario the glider starts at 18 m/s: KE 17.3 J at t=0.02 s (an initial-condition artefact). Steep 28° gives 15.336 J. Dock in wind exceeds 14.9 J in 6/52 sweep runs (max ≈15 J). The KE governor runs at 0.97 of the cap, so ground speed is designed onto the threshold.
findings.recommendedFix: Judge KE over the whole run. Initialise the fast case below the cap or start it from launch. Move the governor to ≤0.9 of the cap, or include gusts in it (it acts on ground speed only).

findings.claim: Wind model: shared makeWind with Taylor advection.
findings.evidence: makeWind advects only along the mean-wind direction. In the crosswind scenarios (mean along y) a glider flying 12 m/s down x samples no spatial turbulence, so the encounter spectrum is under-estimated; this applies to every concept using makeWind. Audit probe with 4 m/s along the fall line at intensity 0.35: avail 87.9 %, airMin 1.04 Vs, minimum height 2.6 m, so the result still passes, with a smaller stall margin.
findings.recommendedFix: Shared model: advect with the flyer's own velocity relative to the air (evaluate wind at p − U·t along the relative-wind vector).

findings.claim: Usability: one gloved tap to arm and one to dock; 2.58 L hip holster.
findings.evidence: A rigid 37 × 8 × 6 cm holster behind the left hip (the gimbal adds height: GM2 is 47 × 47 × 26 mm) conflicts with chairlift seats and T-bars. That is not modelled. After a release, re-clipping a 0.17 mm leash to the hook with gloves needs two bare hands. The snow pull drags the folded glider, with its camera and gimbal, 10–20 m over snow, so abrasion, icing and snow packing into the hinges are not modelled. Launch drags the glider 6.5 m behind the rider at lift exits.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the holster rotatable to the back or side. Use a magnetic hook with a large gloved-hand loop. Add a skid and lens cover on the belly for the snow pull. Package the gimbal inside the fuselage.

findings.claim: Low-Re polar: CD0 0.040 (pod and hinges included), e 0.8, AR 8, CLmax 1.0; L/D 11.2 at 6 m/s and 5.5 at 12 m/s.
findings.evidence: Chord 0.083 m; Re ≈ 29790 at 6 m/s, 59580 at 12 m/s, 84405 at 17 m/s (ρ 1.0, μ 1.67e-5). Closed-form L/Dmax 11.21 at 6.147 m/s matches the model. CD0 0.040 is plausible: a section at 0.015–0.025 near Re 60k (laminar-bubble regime, UIUC LSAT data, https://m-selig.ae.illinois.edu/uiuc_lsat/AirfoilsVolume3.pdf), plus pod (~CDA 4.5e-4 → +0.008), tail and fuselage → 0.040–0.055. At 12 m/s the operating L/D (5.5) is only needed to exceed 1/tan15° = 3.73, and the leash covers the deficit (L/D −30 % still passes, tow share 48 %), so the follow result does not rest on optimistic aero. Weak point: CLmax at Re ≈ 30k is about 0.85, giving Vs ≈ 6.314 m/s rather than 5.82, which erodes the slow-rider and tailwind margin (see TG-02, TG-04).
findings.recommendedFix: Use a Re-dependent CLmax and CD0 (UIUC data for the chosen section) and re-run the tailwind, beginner and stop cases.

findings.claim: jitterRms 1.34 °/s (nominal) / 2.72 °/s (short) passes the ≤3 °/s footage-stability criterion.
findings.evidence: The angular metric is not normalised to the frame. Leapfrog films through a ~6° vertical crop (median cropV nominal 6.431°, short 6.003°), so 1.34 °/s = 20.815 % of frame height per second (short turns 45.354 %/s; independent footageStability subject 1.249 / 2.23 °/s = 19.43 / 37.155 %/s). The 3 °/s line was calibrated on chase framings with ~25–30° crops (≈10–12 %/s). In addition, the glider is a point mass: airframe roll/pitch/yaw in turbulence is not simulated and the 10 g 2-axis turret is credited with an ASSUMED 0.5 °/s residual and perfect world stabilisation (roll unstabilised in hardware). Re-computed footageStability matches the claimed values in all 15 scenarios (e.g. nominal 1.249/0.898).
findings.recommendedFix: Report jitter in % of output frame height per second (or px/s) for all concepts; add airframe attitude dynamics + a turret disturbance-rejection model; loosen framing (fill 0.35 instead of 0.5) for the lead flight.

findings.claim: Native resolution 6144 rows (full 50 MP 1/1.56″ readout) gives a 300 px range of ~66 m, which carries avail and the approach share.
findings.evidence: Quad-Bayer 50 MP sensors (IMX766 class) record video binned (≈12.5 MP, ~3072 rows) or by in-sensor remosaic crop with reduced effective resolution (OVT OV64C brief: hardware remosaic + 2× crop at 16 MP, https://www.ovt.com/sensors/OV64C; IMX766 default binned output, https://zentalk.asus.com/t5/zenfone-9/50mp-camera-resolution/td-p/190258). Re-run with camRows 3072: nominal avail 67.373 % (FAIL), approach share 41.224 %, short 62.683 %, crossgust 39.982 %. With ≈0.7 effective linear resolution (4300 rows): nominal 88.605 %, short 76.41 % (FAIL), crossgust 59.751 %.
findings.recommendedFix: Specify a sensor/ISP that reads the needed window at full resolution at 30 fps (e.g. a 1″-type 20 MP with crop readout) or a longer lens with tighter turret pointing; or shorten the perch gap (fewer but closer shots); re-run with effective rows.

findings.claim: 125 g flying mass (airframe 42, camera+ISP 13, turret+periscope 10, battery 20, hoop 5 g …) keeps KE ≤14.9 J at a 15 m/s ground-speed cap.
findings.evidence: Audit budget from real parts: folding 0.70 m airframe with V-tail, wing-tip skids, belly claws, spring hinges ≈48 g; 1104 motor+4.5″ folding prop+ESC 11 g; FC/IMU/GNSS/UWB/radio/ToF ≈10 g; actuators (4 servos + claw, mast and hoop-shift actuators) ≈16 g; 50 MP tele module ≈4 g + a compute board able to read 50 MP, encode 4K and run tracking ≈11–16 g (ModalAI VOXL 2 Mini 11 g, 0.5–8 W, https://www.modalai.com/products/voxl-2-mini); 2-axis turret + 0.35 m periscope ≈20–25 g (smallest FPV gimbal, CaddxFPV GM1, is 1-axis and 16 g, https://oscarliang.com/caddxfpv-camera-gimbals; a 4K gimbal-less camera RunCam Thumb 2 is 27 g); 1S 3.7 Wh high-C pack ≈24 g (GNB 2S 720 mAh HV = 36 g ≈150 Wh/kg) + self-heating foil; hoop+lanyard+shift ≈7 g; wiring 5 g → ≈160–175 g. At 175 g the KE cap becomes 13.0 m/s (√(2·14.9/0.175)); keeping 15 m/s gives keMax 18.718 J (FAIL). With 175 g and a 13 m/s cap the lead envelope falls from vTarget 14 to 13 m/s, nominal ends with a fall-behind event, touchdown KE exceeds the 3 J design target in every scenario; combined realistic variant (175 g, cd0 0.05, camera 3.5 W, 4300 rows): nominal avail 75.09 % FAIL, short 79.254 % FAIL, endurance 89.455 min.
findings.recommendedFix: Publish a component-level BOM with sourced masses; drop the periscope (perch-height camera on a fixed short mast) or the active hoop; re-derive vCapG from the real mass; keep the 250 g C0 margin.

findings.claim: ops = 2 per run (toss + snatch); lift-queue stow counted as 0 actions.
findings.evidence: criteria.js ops counts 'deploy/launch, stow/land, battery swap, recovery'. The user sequence has three distinct actions: draw+toss (deploy), pole-basket snatch at the run-out (recovery, while moving), unhook from the pole + fold wings + retract hoop/periscope + holster (stow, 6 s standstill already counted in setupTime but 0 actions). Recounted ops = 3 → FAIL (≤2) in every scenario; standstill 4 + 10–15 s gloved stow = 14–19 s still passes ≤30 s. Stranded cases (powder, motor fail, perch failure) are ops 3–4 + detour.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the snatch the stow (hoop pulls the glider straight into a pole-mounted or holster sleeve) or count honestly as 3; measure gloved stow time.

findings.claim: Other skiers are protected by landing-site selection and early hops; KE ≤14.1 J; resort approval is just needed.
findings.evidence: Only one neighbour on a straight track is simulated (nbMin 4.645 m). The device repeatedly lands and sits on the open piste 9–16 m off the rider's line (the lane of other skiers, not the piste edge on a ≤35 m piste), flies at ≤15 m/s, 3 m above snow, approaching downhill skiers from BEHIND (they cannot see it), and the capture perch is placed on the rider's line at the run-out, i.e. the converging lift-approach area. A skier hitting or catching an edge on a 125–175 g perched object is not modelled. Vail Resorts prohibits drones on/over all its properties without written permission, enforced by pass revocation (https://www.vail.com/the-mountain/about-the-mountain/safety/drones.aspx); Alta/Brian Head similar (https://www.skiutah.com/blog/utah-resort-drone-policies). EU A1: C0 may overfly uninvolved persons but never assemblies (UAS.OPEN.020, https://regulatorylibrary.caa.co.uk/2019-947/Content/map/00320_UAS.OPEN.020_UAS_operations_in_subcategory_A1.htm); an unpowered glider is still an unmanned aircraft.
findings.recommendedFix: Model a Poisson field of other skiers (density by piste class) and report collision/near-miss rates; restrict perching to the outer 3 m of the piste; add a no-fly/no-perch rule when skiers are within N m downslope; seek a written resort pilot permission before any field work.

findings.claim: Fault scenarios (powder, motorfail) are 'judged on safety only' and the concept is presented as passing all criteria.
findings.evidence: Powder: avail 44.678 %, approach 33.733 %, ops 3, stranded on the piste ~9 m off the line (manual recovery); motorfail: avail 49.975 %, ops 3. These are not rare faults: soft snow at the piste side after any snowfall, wind-loaded edges and afternoon slush cover the very lane (9–16 m off the rider's line) the glider perches on; ice the opposite failure — with claws not biting (μ≈0.3) a 6 m/s touchdown slides ≈59 m on 15° instead of ≈3.0 m. Snow condition is an operating-envelope variable, not a fault.
findings.recommendedFix: Treat powder/slush/ice as envelope scenarios with harmonised pass/fail; add an in-air hold (lead-only) mode when the snow under the lane is soft, and report the share of resort-days on which perching is possible.

findings.claim: Post-stall perching flare (≈11→5 m/s) and powered take-off from the snow with a nose tractor prop work on groomed snow.
findings.evidence: Both manoeuvres carry the concept and are untested and only point-mass modelled (no pitch dynamics, flat-plate CN = 1.8·sin α ASSUMED, ToF height at 0.5 m over snow spray). Touchdown KE is not dt-converged: nominal 2.22 → 2.57 → 2.83 J at dt 0.01/0.005/0.0025 s (avail and keMax converge to <0.3 %). A 114 mm nose prop on a glider resting on wing-tip skids needs ≥60 mm ground clearance and will ingest spray on a downhill take-off run; take-off needs ≈1.6 N static thrust ≈30 W (9.419 C from a 1000 mAh 1S pack at −10 °C). Cory & Tedrake perched indoors with motion capture.
findings.recommendedFix: Pusher prop on a pylon or above-wing; replace the stall flare by a shallow belly-skid landing with drag skids if tests show flare failures; carry out the listed ≥30-landing test series before any further claims.

findings.claim: Envelope: wind ≤10 m/s mean, crosswind gusts handled; nominal results robust.
findings.evidence: Wind-seed sweep (12 seeds, same scenario otherwise): nominal avail 94.162–95.962 % (robust); short 81.964–87.606 %; headwind 6 m/s 65.26–97.734 % (fails a standard metric in 17 % of seeds); crossgust 6+7 m/s 36.428–89.827 % (fails in 42 %; sepMax >50 m in 7/12, tdKE >3 J in 4/12); perchwind fails in 83 %. The concept-specific shotsPerMin ≥2/min passes with skier seed 1 only and fails with 7 of 8 other skier seeds (the default skier seed is favourable; non-harmonised criterion).
findings.recommendedFix: State the envelope as mean wind ≤4–6 m/s; report seed distributions (p10) instead of one seed.

findings.claim: results.json and design_notes.json numbers for crossgust and perchwind.
findings.evidence: Stale: common/env.js was modified at 20:25 after results.json (20:19). Re-run gives crossgust avail 76.1 % (claimed 71.2), endurance 110 min (83), frontShare 57 % (51); perchwind perchSF 1.32 (claimed 1.121), it now takes off once (keMax 13.7 J vs 0, sepMax 96 m vs 246). Pass/fail flags of the 12 harmonised metrics unchanged. All other scenarios reproduce exactly.
findings.recommendedFix: Re-run run_all.mjs after shared-model changes and regenerate design_notes.json numbers.

findings.claim: Endurance 117 min nominal (≥45 min) with the 3.7 Wh on-board cell + 10 Wh holster bank at −10 °C ×0.75, 10 % reserve.
findings.evidence: Formula reproduced (116.86 min). Camera+ISP at 1.7 W is optimistic for a 50 MP readout + 4K encode + vision tracking (VOXL 2 Mini class 0.5–8 W). With +1.8 W and an 85 % bank→cell transfer: nominal 75.458 min, gentle 6° 51.7 min, headwind 6 m/s 40.138 min (FAIL <45). Per run the on-board cell suffices (≈0.273 Wh of 2.498 Wh usable). Charging Li-ion at −10 °C on the lift relies on the self-heating cell (heating energy not counted, ≈0.1 Wh/cycle).
findings.recommendedFix: Use a measured power figure for the chosen compute/camera; count bank transfer and heater losses.

findings.claim: Capture: active 0.4 m hoop hit 98.9 % at 4 m/s, 99.99 % with the automatic second pass.
findings.evidence: Hit rate depends entirely on the ASSUMED pole-aim scatter σ_lat = 0.035+0.013·v (no data). Re-computed MC: at 5 m/s ×1 0.972, ×1.5 0.833, ×2 0.644; at 4 m/s ×2 0.742. A miss costs ~17 s of riding (no standstill) plus another landing 0.7 m from the rider's line. Snatch loads are benign (3.7 N at 4 m/s, 9.2 N at 8 m/s; 39.6 N at 10 m/s when the lanyard bottoms); claws still engaged add ≈4.355 N break-out at 0.436 m stretch – no problem.
findings.recommendedFix: Bench-test pole-basket aim with 10 skiers at 2–8 m/s (kill if σ_lat >0.12 m at 5 m/s, as the notes propose).

findings.claim: Scope: the perch mode is 'borderline' against docs/19 and left to the product owner.
findings.evidence: docs/19 excludes '提前沿途放置相机及依赖专用停栖设施的系统。即使由本人预放相机，也按环境机位排除' and keeps '本人携带并自主随行的飞行相机、雪面设备'. Leapfrog is carried by the user, places itself during the run (not in advance, not by hand), uses no dedicated perch facility and is within ≤50 m (nominal) of the rider; perched share is 7.5 % of skiing time nominal, 20–24 % for slow riders. Auditor reading: IN SCOPE as an autonomous accompanying flying camera; R06 differs because it is hand-thrown and static. Caveat: a stranded device (powder, motor failure, perch failure) becomes a left-behind object and must be retrieved by the user, which docs/19 counts in the 'failure recovery burden'.
findings.recommendedFix: Product owner to confirm; keep lead-only (V1) as the fallback if perching is ruled out.

findings.claim: Regulation: EU C0/A1 with follow-me ≤50 m; US recreational <250 g; VLOS is easier because the device is in front.
findings.evidence: Correct in substance: a privately built <250 g UA may fly in A1; camera → operator registration; follow-me derogation to 50 m from the remote pilot (UAS.OPEN.020(3)). The 50 m limit is exceeded in crossgust (sepMax 53 m) and perchwind (96 m), and in 7/12 crossgust seeds. FAA: recreational <250 g needs no registration/Remote ID but TRUST, CBO guidelines and VLOS of the operator (https://www.faa.gov/uas/recreational_flyers); a lead device in front of the skier is the one aerial layout where VLOS is plausibly kept. Resort bans dominate (LF-05).
findings.recommendedFix: Hard-limit separation to 50 m in the controller (land rather than exceed).

findings.claim: Usability: 2 actions, 10 s standstill, 2.6 L holster, one gloved hand.
findings.evidence: Holster 0.38 × 0.085 × 0.08 m = 2.58 L reproduced; credible only if the fuselage incl. folded prop is ≤0.36 m and the 0.4 m hoop and 0.35 m periscope telescope/fold inside. A 38 cm rigid holster on the hip sits on the chairlift seat edge. Stow at the lift queue (unhook from pole basket, fold two spring-loaded wings, retract hoop and mast, insert) with gloves is more likely 10–15 s than 6 s. The run-out snatch requires the rider to slow to 4–5 m/s on a predictable line – a riding constraint at every run end. Morning/evening USB-C charging of two devices.
findings.recommendedFix: Prototype a holster mock-up and time 10 gloved users; consider a back-of-pack sleeve.

findings.claim: Aero: Re 50–150 k, L/D 7–12, CLmax 1.0, gravity pays the cruise on ≥15°.
findings.evidence: Re-derived: span 0.7 m, chord 0.079 m, Re = 37658–65902 at 8–14 m/s (−10 °C) – i.e. 33–66 k, BELOW the brief's 50–150 k band at the slow end. L/D used at operating speed is modest and not inflated: 7.0 at 12 m/s (CL 0.31), 5.4 at 14 m/s; LDmax 11.8 only at 6.9 m/s, just above stall (6.7 m/s) and never used. cd0 0.040 lies inside an audit build-up of 0.030–0.045 (UIUC LSAT airfoil cd 0.015–0.022 at Re 40–60 k, https://m-selig.ae.illinois.edu/uiuc_lsat.html). CLmax 1.0 at Re ≈35 k is at the upper end for a thin folding wing. Glide angle 8.1° at 12 m/s; with L/D −30 % at 14 m/s 14.9° ≈ slope, so the motor fills in (nominal_ld70 motor 2.8 W, still passes). Credible.
findings.recommendedFix: Use Re-dependent polars (cd rising below Re 50 k) for slow phases (landing, short turns).

findings.claim: 8.5 Wh battery weighs 22 g (380 Wh/kg at pack level), giving a 124 g flying mass and 50.5 min endurance at -10 C.
findings.evidence: 380 Wh/kg pack level is better than any small cell shipping today. Amprius SiCore is 370 Wh/kg at cell level (2025) and 500 Wh/kg is announced for Q4 2026 in sUAS pouch formats (https://dronelife.com/2026/09/02/amprius-drone-battery-longer-flights-500-wh-kg/ , https://www.militaryaerospace.com/power/article/55261937/amprius-unveils-high-energy-sicore-battery-cell-for-aviation-and-electric-mobility); neither is a ~1.2 Ah micro pack. Real micro 2S LiPo: 520 mAh = 3.85 Wh at 33 g, about 117 Wh/kg (https://www.fpv24.com/en/boslipo/boslipo-p7-battery-520mah-74v-2s-95c-lipo-battery-with-xt30-plug). Audit runs: the same 22 g at 200 Wh/kg gives 4.5 Wh and nominal endurance 26.2 min (claimed 50.5, fail). Keeping 8.5 Wh at 200 Wh/kg gives a 144.5 g aircraft. Its KE-cap speed drops from 14.24 to 13.21 m/s, so nominal avail falls to 79.9 % and full-cycle avail to 24.0 % (claimed 65). At 150 Wh/kg (158.7 g) nominal avail is 43.7 % and cycle avail 2.9 %.
findings.recommendedFix: Use 200-250 Wh/kg (best small Li-ion/Si pouch, ASSUMED) as the base case and keep 380 as an upside variant. Re-close the loop between mass, KE cap and endurance.

findings.claim: A gravity-paid follow with autonomous relaunch from the snow catches up with the rider (2-4 s, or 8-12 s at full speed).
findings.evidence: The ground-speed cap 0.92*sqrt(2*14.9/m) is only about 2 m/s above a 12 m/s rider. After a launch from standstill the glider closes the gap at about 1 m/s, so catch-up depends on mass. Cycle (2 m/s wind) avail with extra mass: +0 g 65.2 %, +10 g 51.7 %, +20 g 24.3 %, +28 g 5.5 % (pxMed 359 -> 198 px). With the audit's realistic build (152.5 g, 3.3 W avionics, FoM*eta 0.35) nominal avail is 64.1 %, cycle avail 5.4 %, stop avail 50.4 % and gust avail 56.2 %. The 14.9 J line is a project criterion (FAA Part 107 Cat 2 analogue), not a legal limit for a sub-250 g C0 aircraft.
findings.recommendedFix: Choose one of three: (a) a mass budget of 125 g or less that is actually achievable, (b) a justified KE allowance during catch-up only (e.g. ≤25 J when more than 10 m from anyone, with ranging), or (c) accept that the first 10-20 s after each launch or stop is lost and count it. Report avail on the full cycle, not on the 30 s nominal.

findings.claim: Standstill per run is 17 s (90th percentile over 0-9 m/s wind) and ops = 2.
findings.evidence: SETUP_SWEEP = 17 comes from three hand-picked cycles: 2 m/s, 5 m/s seed 6, and 9 m/s blowing UP-slope/cross ([-6, 6.7]), which avoids the tailwind abort. The audit swept 51 full cycles (0/3/5/7/9 m/s x tail/cross/head/diagonal-tail x 3 seeds). setupTime p90 under the concept's own rule is 34 s (fail ≤30). With recovery of tipped or off-track gliders counted (+15 s for righting, +60 s for walking to an off-track landing, both ASSUMED) it is 109 s. ops > 2 in 33 % of runs. Every run with a tailwind component of about 5 m/s or more aborts (avail 0-13 %). The full-cycle avail median is 55.7 % and only 8 % of cycles reach 80 %. The palm launch (used above ~6 m/s) passes the props within 0.5 m of the helmet in 6/24 windy cycles, including the claimed cycle_w9 at 0.14 m.
findings.recommendedFix: Report setupTime/ops as the p90 over a direction-randomised wind sweep, including recovery. Fix the palm-launch geometry (arm's-length side release or ground plant only). State the tailwind ≤5 m/s envelope as a hard limit.
findings.fixableNote: partly (tailwind window is physics: 1.3 Vs to KE-cap airspeed)

findings.claim: The nominal scenario (12/12 pass) represents the product.
findings.evidence: Nominal is 30 s and starts already in follow mode (2 s settle discarded). It has no launch, stop or landing and uses light 2 m/s wind; it is the only scenario family where avail ≥80 is robust (12 seeds: 85.4-88.4 %). Realistic sequences fail avail under the concept's own model: stop 59.9-63.1 % over 12 seeds (0/12 pass), short turns 73-75 %, moguls 66 %, trees 78 %, cycle 65 % / cycle_w5 71 % (12 seeds: 4.9-74.5 %, ops 3 in 3/12) / cycle_w9 54 %, fast (18 m/s) 9 %, steep 26° at 14 m/s 10 %, tailwind 6 m/s 4.7 %. Endurance passes only in light wind: gust 33.7 (12 seeds 26-33.7), headwind 23.5, stop_windy 24.7, cycle_w9 18.6 min.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the full cycle (plant, launch, follow with 1-2 stops, land) the headline scenario. Quote the envelope rather than the 12/12 nominal.

findings.claim: Endurance 50.5 min at -10 C includes the per-run hover phases.
findings.evidence: Formula: Euse = 8.5 Wh*0.75*0.85 = 19.5 kJ over (pFollow*150 s + 334 J). It assumes 150 filmed s and exactly one mid-run perch per run. Perched and landed camera time (0.85*2.6 W) is excluded. Hover uses FoM*eta = 0.5 (14.6 W). Recomputed: two stops per run gives 44.5 min; two stops with FoM*eta 0.35 (20.9 W hover, typical of 4-inch micro props with 1103-class motors) gives 37.7 min. Camera at 3.3 W: nominal 45.6, stop 40.4 min. dt is not converged (pFollow 4.21 -> 3.54 W from dt 4 -> 1 ms). That error is in the conservative direction (+12 % endurance).
findings.recommendedFix: Count the stops per run from a realistic run profile (2-4). Use FoM*eta 0.35-0.4. Include camera-on standstill time. Use dt ≤2 ms for the energy ledger.

findings.claim: Mass budget: 4K pan-tilt ball camera 18 g at 1.6 W; FC/IMU/GNSS/UWB/radio/ToF 10 g at 0.7 W; 2x 1103 + ESC + 4-inch folding props 17 g giving 2.6 N static.
findings.evidence: RunCam Thumb Pro 4K is 16 g and 2.5 W max (500 mA at 5 V) with no gimbal (https://www.getfpv.com/runcam-thumb-pro-4k-hd-action-camera-wide-fov.html). Thumb 2 is 27 g and 3.5 W max (https://www.getfpv.com/runcam-thumb-2-4k-hd-action-camera.html). A 2-axis pan-tilt adds about 6-10 g. Subject tracking on 4K plus 12 m forward ranging (e.g. a TFmini-class lidar about 5 g) needs a vision SoC that is not in the budget (+5-10 g, +1-2 W). The 1103 is a 2-inch-class motor: Sub250 1103 14000KV gives about 101 g at 70 % on a 1.6-inch tri-blade at 1.74 g/W (https://rcdrone.top/products/sub250-1103-14000kv-motor). 4-inch folding props need a 1404-class motor (about +8 g total). Audit estimate: 155-170 g with an 8.5 Wh pack at 200 Wh/kg. That is still under 250 g (C0), but see DG-01/DG-02.
findings.recommendedFix: Rebuild the mass and power budget from datasheet parts, including a vision/ranging compute line item, and rerun at the resulting mass.

findings.claim: Upright tail-down perch in the snow: tip-over wind 11.7 m/s (span aligned) / 8.2 m/s (15° off); 0 W waiting.
findings.evidence: The tip-over threshold falls quickly once the wind is off the span axis: 30° 6.7, 45° 5.9, 90° 5.2 m/s at the body, and 4.5-7.0 m/s on ice (anchor moment 0). The perch yaw is frozen at touchdown, so a wind shift of 30-45° during a 14 s stop halves the margin. The snow-spike anchor (0.03 N*m, about 26 % of the restoring moment) is ASSUMED with no test. Slope tilt, soft-snow sinking and the downwash brownout or icing during hover landings on fresh snow are not modelled. The wait is not 0 W: the camera runs at 0.85*2.6 W.
findings.recommendedFix: Bench and field tests: perch stability vs wind angle on groomed, powder and ice; snow recirculation in hover landings. Allow re-yaw while perched (a servo) or lay it flat in wind.

findings.claim: Safety and regulation: C0 under 250 g, Open A1 follow-me; bystander KE ≤14.9 J.
findings.evidence: KE recomputed under the criteria rule (ground frame beyond 1.5 m): it matches the claim in every scenario (max 13.4 J fast, 12.4 nominal). The design_notes regulation section is honest. EU 2019/947 lets follow-me waive VLOS only within 50 m of the remote pilot (https://regulatorylibrary.caa.co.uk/2019-947/Content/map/00320_UAS.OPEN.020_UAS_operations_in_subcategory_A1.htm), yet the model lets it trail 66-133 m behind (steep, fast) with no 50 m leash. In the US, 49 USC 44809 has no follow-me exception, so a solo skier is out of VLOS. Vail Resorts bans drones on all its properties and penalises with pass revocation; other resorts require written permission (https://www.vail.com/the-mountain/about-the-mountain/safety/drones.aspx , https://www.skiutah.com/blog/utah-resort-drone-policies). The landing 'beside you at the lift' is in a lift-queue area, plausibly an assembly of people. A perched 0.3 m spiked glider 5.5 m down-slope on the piste is an obstacle for other skiers, and it relaunches with props spinning when 'the rider moves'.
findings.recommendedFix: Add a 50 m range fail-safe (perch). Land at a geofenced point off the lift maze. Perch at the piste edge, not on the fall line. Use guarded or ducted props for hops near people. Treat resort permission as a gating item.
findings.fixableNote: partly (resort bans and FAA VLOS are not engineering-fixable)

findings.claim: Aero: L/D_max 7.9 (spread) / 6.7 (swept), CLmax 1.0 / 0.8, stall 6.2 / 9.2 m/s.
findings.evidence: Recomputed exactly: AR 6.41, e 0.75, CD0 0.060, L/D_max 7.93 at CL 0.95 and 6.4 m/s. Re is 49-91 k (spread) and 43-80 k (swept) at 8-15 m/s (nu = 1.59e-5 at rho 1.05). CD0 0.06 including nacelles, fins and the ball camera is conservative, and the -30 % L/D sensitivity was run (endurance 38.9, fail): credible and honest. CLmax 1.0 is optimistic for a reflexed tailless wing with overlapping feather panels at Re ≈50-70 k. Reflexed sections at this Re reach about 0.8-0.9 and trimmed tailless CLmax is lower (UIUC low-speed airfoil data, https://m-selig.ae.illinois.edu/uiuc_lsat.html; ASSUMED reading). CLmax 0.8 raises spread stall to about 7.0 m/s, which affects short turns, moguls and flat track.
findings.recommendedFix: Use CLmax 0.8 (spread) / 0.65 (swept) as the base case for a reflexed feather wing and rerun short/moguls/flat.

findings.claim: Footage stability.
findings.evidence: The independent footageStability(R) subject RMS is ≤2.22 deg/s in every scenario (nominal 0.65, short 1.44, moguls 1.76, cycle_w5 2.22), consistent with the claimed jitterRms 0.52-1.17. Background RMS is 4.03 (short) and 3.95 (moguls), above the ideal chase reference of 1.6-3.0 deg/s; it is not a gated criterion. The 0.5 deg/s EIS residual added in quadrature is ASSUMED.
findings.recommendedFix: None required. Report backgroundRms next to jitter.

findings.claim: dt / reproducibility.
findings.evidence: rerun_descentglider/results.json is identical to dev results.json, apart from compute times. Tests pass 18/18. At dt 4 -> 2 -> 1 ms: nominal avail 85.4/84.7/84.0, pFollow 4.21/3.67/3.54 W. Stop and gust are converged within 2 % on avail.
findings.recommendedFix: Use dt 2 ms for energy metrics.

findings.claim: Packed volume 2.32 L (flat sleeve 14.5x5x32 cm), 2 gloved actions.
findings.evidence: Geometry is plausible: feathers fold along a 0.32 m fuselage and the X fins span 0.14 m. Planting a tail-spiked 124 g carbon glider upright with gloves (4 s) and picking it up (5 s) are ASSUMED durations; both are only illustrated. Hand-launch (windy) puts props near the face. The UWB tag must be worn (12 g).
findings.recommendedFix: A gloved handling mock-up test. Fold the feathers automatically on insertion.

findings.claim: The three gliders share one battery/aero basis (DEV_BRIEF_GLIDER: "use these common assumptions so the three are comparable").
findings.evidence: Flying-cell specific energy: towglider 150 Wh/kg, leapfrog 185 Wh/kg, descentglider 380 Wh/kg (2–2.5× the others; real micro 2S packs ≈117–200 Wh/kg, DG-01). Reserve 10 % (tow, leap) vs 15 % (descent). ρ 1.0 (tow, leap, kite) vs 1.05 (descent: −2.4 % stall speed). CD0 0.040 (tow, leap) vs 0.060 (descent). Camera power for the same RunCam-Thumb class module: 1.6 W (descent), 1.7 W (leap), 2.5 W (tow, kite); audit sources give 2.5 W max at 5 V.
findings.recommendedFix: Put one shared table in common/ (cell Wh/kg ≤200 pack-level, camera 2.5 W, ρ 1.0 at 2000–2500 m/−10 °C, reserve 15 %, cold 0.75, no charging below 0 °C unless heated) and re-run all concepts.

findings.claim: Flying masses 62 / 95 / 125 / 124 g.
findings.evidence: Every concept is under-budgeted by 20–40 % against real components (RunCam Thumb Pro 16 g/2.5 W; smallest brushless 2-axis micro gimbal found ≈30 g, Caddx GM2; 1103 motors are 2-inch class, 4-inch props need 1404; vision/ranging compute missing): kite 75–113 g, tow 117–125 g, leap 160–175 g, descent 152–167 g. Because each glider caps ground speed at √(2·14.9 J/m), mass directly shrinks the follow envelope (tow 17.7→16.0 m/s, leap 15→≈13 m/s, descent 14.2→12.9 m/s) and the catch-up margin after launch.
findings.recommendedFix: Shared component library with sourced masses; carry ≥15 % margin; re-run envelopes at the audit masses.

findings.claim: Endurance ≥45 min at −10 °C (kite 258, tow 102, leap 117, descent 50.5 min).
findings.evidence: Kite, tow and leap reach the target only by recharging the flying cell from a worn bank on every lift ride (Li-ion must not be charged below ≈0 °C; tow needs ≈1.9 C): glider-only tow 10.9 min, kite sortie 12 min at 3.5 W camera. Descent has no bank and passes only at 380 Wh/kg and one stop per run (26 min at 200 Wh/kg). Endurance definitions therefore differ (kite counts a 30 Wh pack; descent counts only the aircraft).
findings.recommendedFix: Use one endurance definition: everything worn, −10 °C, 15 % reserve, cold-charge only into a heated cell with its heater energy charged to the budget, power from a harmonised full-run scenario with stops.

findings.claim: "nominal" represents normal use.
findings.evidence: No concept's nominal includes a stop; descentglider's does not include launch either. Where audited, stop-including runs fail avail: kite stop-start 76.9 %, descent stop 59.9–63.1 % (0/12 seeds) and full cycle 54–71 %, leap powder 44.7 %; setupTime p90 was computed by each concept on 2–3 hand-picked winds (audit sweeps: kite 17 s, tow 21 s, leap 14–19 s, descent 34 s).
findings.recommendedFix: Add a shared "fullRun" scenario (top deploy → 2 stops → lift-approach stow, 12 wind seeds 0–9 m/s × 4 directions) and judge avail/setupTime/ops/endurance on it.

findings.claim: Jitter/footageStability passes (all concepts ≤3 °/s).
findings.evidence: Independent footageStability recomputations agree with the claims (kite 0.21/0.45 °/s nominal, tow 0.97/1.12, leap 1.25 nominal / 2.23 short, descent subject ≤2.22, background up to 4.0 in short turns/moguls), but the gliders are point-mass (or lagged-attitude) models with an assumed ideal or fixed-residual gimbal: airframe pitch/roll/yaw response to turbulence is not simulated, so the pass is by construction for the gliders. Leapfrog's ≈6° crop makes 1.25 °/s ≈21 %/s of frame height.
findings.recommendedFix: Add attitude dynamics + a gimbal bandwidth/residual model shared by all gliders, and normalise jitter by crop FOV (%/s of frame).

findings.claim: All four are acceptable on safety/regulation as noted in design_notes.
findings.evidence: All three gliders are UAS (EU C0 needs <250 g and toy/C0 marking; with a camera the operator must register; A1 follow-me only within 50 m — descent trails 66–133 m with no 50 m fail-safe). US recreational rules need VLOS by the operator or a co-located observer, which a solo downhill skier with a follower behind cannot keep (tow, descent); leapfrog flies ahead and is the best case. Vail Resorts bans drones without written permission. kite2 is not aviation-regulated below 25 kg (EU) / 5 lb (FAA Part 101) but resorts such as Aspen and Niseko Hirafu ban kiting on pistes, and its line is 1.15–1.72 m above snow 1–2 m behind the rider.
findings.recommendedFix: Treat resort written permission as a gate for every concept; design to C0/<250 g with Remote-ID-free class; add a 50 m leash/geofence; for kite2 a breakaway, high-visibility line and no-follower-within-5 m sensing.

findings.claim: results.json files reflect the current shared models.
findings.evidence: sim/js/concepts/common/env.js changed at 2026-10-19 20:25:04, after kite2 (20:18), leapfrog (20:19) and towglider (20:24) results were written.
